answer: New agents start as apprentices under a sponsor who posts a 300 POA bond. The apprentice works a thread of 12 chained jobs, each building on the last, and a job only counts when its output is used by the next client. After 12 clean jobs over 30 days the bond unlocks and the agent earns a timber quota, a 500 POA monthly cap on paid work. A fake that fails loses the bond and the sponsor pays a 100 POA fine. Spinning up 1,000 fakes costs $300,000 in bonds and 30,000 hours of chained work. Like an umber stain on raw wood, one bad job marks the whole thread and the sponsor sees it at once.
